later_events.mechanism: amendment by word substitution: section 2-101 of EO 12107 substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission and the Director of that Office for the Chairman in each listed order, and EO 11355 is listed in subsection 2-101(b); section 2-404 says "Order, this Order shall be effective on January 1, 1979.". Before: clause 1 makes the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission responsible for the annual survey; after: the Director, Office of Personnel Management carries that duty (the exact post-substitution wording is not printed in the held sources). The substitution does not touch clauses 2 and 3, which name no Commission or Chairman.

clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12919, section 904(a): the list that follows the words "are superseded or revoked:" includes, as item (6), "Executive Order No. 11355 of May 26, 1967 (32 FR 7803)"; EO 12919 contains no effective-date wording in its sections 901-905, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, June 3, 1994 (59 FR 29525, printed June 7, 1994). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
clauses.reason: Clause 1 rewrites the first sentence of subsection 305(a) of EO 10647 so that the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission surveys, at least once every twelve months, appointments made under section 710(b)(1) of the Act. It continued, amended, until the order ended: first end EO 12919, 1994-06-03, which supersedes or revokes EO 11355 by number in section 904(a)(6). EO 12107 later substituted Office of Personnel Management words for the Commission and Chairman effective 1979-01-01 (a later event, not an end; the clause text before the substitution is quoted in the clause's original text and the after-effect is that the Director of the Office carries the survey duty). EO 10647 was revoked by the same section.

It continued, amended, until the order ended: first end EO 12919, 1994-06-03, section 904(a)(6). The held clause text stops at the word positions because the printed closing punctuation is missing from the extracted text. clauses.reason: Clause 3 revokes Part II of EO 10647. It is a self-executing revocation that took effect with the order (1967-05-26, the date the order was signed and filed). It is recorded as ending with the order, first end EO 12919, 1994-06-03, because no held source shows that the command ended earlier and EO 12919 revoked EO 11355 by name; the surviving consequence (Part II of EO 10647 stays revoked) is an accrued result. EO 10647 was itself revoked by the same section.

research_rationale:
EO 11355 (1967-05-26, 32 FR 7803) amends EO 10647 of November 28, 1955 on appointments under the Defense Production Act of 1950: clause 1 rewrites the first sentence of subsection 305(a) (annual survey by the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission of appointments under section 710(b)(1) of the Act), clause 2 rewrites paragraph (1) of subsection 305(b) (the statistical report) and clause 3 revokes Part II of EO 10647. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11355.txt, 32 FR 7803, PDF pages 7-7) and confirmed its number, title and date against the census register; the three numbered clauses are the complete inventory, and the opening authority paragraph is a lead-in, not a command. EO 12919 (signed 1994-06-03) supersedes or revokes EO 10647 and EO 11355 by number in section 904(a), and the dossier carries the ACT record for it. The first end of every clause is that express revocation. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments each amending clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends; EO 10647 ended by the same section on the same date. EO 12107 (signed 1978-12-28) later substituted Office of Personnel Management words in EO 11355 and is recorded as a later event of clause 1, not an end. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

savings.reason: EO 12919 has no savings clause for revoked orders as such, but section 903 says nothing in that order shall affect the validity or force of anything done under previous delegations or other assignment of authority; surveys, reports and appointments made under EO 10647 as amended by this order are therefore accrued completed acts. The commands themselves do not continue because section 904(a) revokes them by name.
